title: Cold fusion / LENR reevaluation: replication failure, high-rigor re-test, and residual materials-science questions
summary: A replication-program record for the cold-fusion trajectory. Encodes the 1989 claim, subsequent reproduction failure and skepticism, and a later high-rigor multi-institution reevaluation that had not yielded evidence while still producing materials-science insights.

status_history.note: Seed flagged cold fusion as a famous failure-of-replication case with later subculture and nuance.

place.scope: Cold fusion / LENR research-program and replication context

claims.claim: The Nature 2019 perspective describes the 1989 cold-fusion claim as publicly heralded and says subsequent failures to reproduce the effect heightened skepticism and contributed to the subject’s disqualification.
what_would_change_status: A historical review with better source depth materially changes the summary of post-1989 replication failure and skepticism.

claims.claim: The 2019 multi-institution reevaluation described in Nature says the effort had yet to yield evidence for cold fusion/LENR despite high-rigor testing.
what_would_change_status: A later peer-reviewed program report produces credible evidence under comparable or stronger controls.

claims.claim: The record’s status must preserve residual scope: the 2019 source says the work nevertheless produced insights into hydrided metals and LENR parameter space, so the cube should not encode the case as “no interesting materials science here.”
what_would_change_status: A second-pass review finds the residual-learning claim is overstated or not supported by the source.

limitations: Original 1989 publication and DOE report full text are not extracted in this revision.
LENR subculture, later claimed positives, and methodological disagreements are not adjudicated.

type_payload.replication_program: Cold-fusion/LENR high-rigor reevaluation as summarized in Nature 2019, contextualized by DOE 1989 review metadata.
type_payload.original_sampling_frame: 1989 Fleischmann–Pons claim and immediate follow-up/replication attempts as cited by the 2019 review; not fully extracted here.

replication_metrics.result_summary: 2019 perspective says reevaluation had yet to yield evidence for LENR/cold fusion.
replication_metrics.metric_grain: qualitative program-level result; not a Many Labs-style effect-size replication record.

status_cautions: Does not adjudicate every LENR claim or every later experiment.
Does not collapse replication failure into fraud.
Preserves collateral materials-science learning and parameter-space mapping.

handling_notes: Avoid ridicule framing; distinguish extraordinary claim, replication failure, and continuing fringe/subfield disputes.
Do not use the record to imply all unconventional research is worthless.

unknowns: Full DOE 1989 report extraction remains open.
Original Fleischmann/Pons publication and early negative replications are not separately promoted yet.
No sociological/genealogy record for LENR subculture yet.
next_actions: Promote the DOE 1989 report as a full program-audit record if source access permits.
Add original publication and early replication attempts with exact bibliographic extraction.
Add a sociology/genealogy record on persistence of LENR communities only with careful neutral tone.
